# Pathway header bytes from the official Datadog tracers and from the wire-format
# primitives they share. The expected fields of each entry come from the reference
# implementation, not from reading the header back with this library, so the
# codec is checked against the wire format rather than against itself.
#
# dd-trace-go v2, commit e5c3c1ce53fbc9e6399129a3078cdae9136e2b85. A throw-away
# test in the package built the unexported Pathway value and called
# EncodeBase64/DecodeBase64 from internal/datastreams/propagator.go.
#
# dd-trace-py, commit 0729596a96039adcd4934e58f9a679ce1b15ed0f. The :python
# entries encode struct.pack("<Q", hash) followed by encode_var_int_64/1 for the
# two timestamps, which is DataStreamsCtx.encode in
# internal/datastreams/processor.py. The :python_test_suite entry is a literal
# header from that repository's tests/datastreams/test_botocore.py, i.e. a value
# a real tracer propagated.
#
# dd-trace-java, commit e1b76dbfba85c5ef9f36d65992fcf9430aa7cad5. Its
# DefaultPathwayContext.encode writes the hash with writeLongLE, the two
# millisecond values with VarEncodingHelper.encodeSignedVarLong and base64s the
# buffer. Building the tracer needs its full Gradle build, so the :java entries
# below are derived analytically from that source, not captured from a running
# JVM tracer; each states the value it encodes. Two of them coincide with :go
# entries because both tracers share this wire format.
#
# The nine-byte entries use timestamps of 2^56 ms, far past any wall clock, to
# exercise the widest varint the format allows.
[
  %{
    source: :go,
    provenance: "dd-trace-go Pathway{hash: 234} EncodeBase64()",
    base64: "6gAAAAAAAACAoKv++WKA2uKB+mI=",

    pathway_start: 1_700_000_000_000,
    edge_start: 1_700_003_600_000
  },
